div.ab: Ærest þæt mon ne sparige nænne þeof þe æt hæbbendre honda gefongen sy, ofer XII winter ⁊ ofer eahta peningas.
Be ðeofum. Ærest ðet man ne spa[rige] nanne ðeof ðe æt hæbbendre hand gefangen sy, ofer twelf winterne ⁊ ofer eahta penegas.
An ærest þæt mon ne sparige nanne þeof þe æt hæbbendre handa gefangen sie, ofer twelf winter and ofer VIII peningas.
De eo, quod non parcatur alicui latroni ad habentem manum. Inprimis est, ut non parcatur alicui latroni ađ manum habenti, si capiatur, supra XII annos et VIII denarios.
[Be ðeofum.] Ærest þæt mon ne sparige nænne þeof þe æt hæbbendre honda gefongen sy, ofer XII winter ⁊ ofer eahta peningas.
(Von Dieben. B) Erstens, dass man keinen Dieb schone, der bei handhafter That gefangen wird, [wenn er] über 12 Jahr und [das Gestohlene] über 8 Pfennige [ist].
(Of thieves. B) First, that no thief be spared who is caught in the act, [if he is] over 12 years and [the stolen goods are] over 8 pence.
First, no thief shall be spared, who is seized in the act, if he is over twelve years old and [if the value of the stolen goods is] more than 8 pence.
Concerning thieves. First, that no thief is to be spared who is caught with the stolen goods, [if he is] over twelve years and [if the value of the goods is] over eightpence.

note.label: changes age
note.quote: Highly suggestive is the re-appearance in this context of the age of twelve. Ine had made ten the age when one might be accessory to theft.

note.label: like
note.quote: convicted thieves get forty days in prison, like breakers of Alfred’s að 7 wed (1, 5)

note.quote: II As. 6:3 ... shows that the 120 shillings of excerpt 5 applied only if no damage was done

note.label: raises age
note.quote: the king and his witan eventually found it ‘cruel (hreowlic)’ to kill those so young, and raised the age to fifteen

note.label: winter
note.seg: winterne. B, Ld, and originally H [Schmid].

This code covers many of the main problems faced by English kings in their attempts to preserve good order. It is later than the accession of Archbishop Wulfhelm, probably in 926, and earlier than several other codes of Athelstan, which refer back to it. It survives in Textus Roffensis and C.C.C.C., MS. 383; there are fragments of B.L.Cott. Otho B. xi, in a late-eleventh-century hand, and it is in Nowell's transcript of this.'It is in Quadripartitus. The text is edited by Liebermann, I, 150–67; and by Attenborough, with English translation, pp. 126–43; by Thorpe, I, 194–215. [Her footnote 2: This heading is in Textus Roffensis only. C.C.C.C., MS. 383, has “Concerning Thieves”.]
literally, “that one has a clean back”
